<h>Lectio 1</h>
Léctio sancti Evangélii secúndum Matthǽum
<r>Matt 21:33-46</r>
<c>I</c>n illo témpore: Dixit Jesus turbis Judæórum, et princípibus sacerdótum parábolam hanc: Homo erat paterfamílias, qui plantávit víneam, et sepem circúmdedit ei. Et réliqua.

Homilía sancti Ambrósii Epíscopi
<r>Lib. 9 in cap. 20 Lucæ</r>
<c>P</c>leríque várias significatiónes de víneæ appellatióne derívant: sed evidénter Isaías víneam Dómini Sábaoth, domum Israël esse memorávit. Hanc víneam quis álius, nisi Deus, cóndidit? Hic est ergo qui eam locávit colónis, et ipse péregre fuit: non quia ex loco ad locum proféctus est Dóminus, qui ubíque semper præsens est: sed quia est præséntior diligéntibus, negligéntibus abest.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Quis igitur ille est qui dudum captam venatiónem áttulit mihi, et comédi ex ómnibus priúsquam tu venires?
* Benedixique ei, et erit benedictus.
<r>℣.</r> Dóminum tuum illum constítui, et omnes fratres ejus servitúti illíus subjugávi.
<r>℟.</r> Benedixique ei, et erit benedictus.

<h>Reading 1</h>
Continuation of the Holy Gospel according to Matthew
<r>Matt 21:33-46</r>
<c>I</c>n that time, Jesus said to the multitude of Jews and the chief priests: Hear ye another parable. There was a man an householder, who planted a vineyard, and made a hedge round about it. And so on.

Homily by St. Ambrose, Bishop <n>of Milan.</n>
<r>Bk. ix on Luke xx</r>
<c>M</c>any derive diverse spiritual meanings from the term vineyard, but Isaias giveth us to know that the vineyard of the Lord of Sabaoth is the house of Israel. <n>v. 7.</n> Who but God planted that vineyard? He it was that let it out to husbandmen, and went into a far country; not that the Lord, Who is everywhere present, moveth from place to place; but because He is nigh unto them that seek Him, and from such as regard Him not He standeth afar off. For a long time He tarried away, lest He might seem to ask too early for the fruits of His vineyard. For where kindness is greatest, there ingratitude is worst.
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> Quis igitur ille est qui dudum captam venatiónem áttulit mihi, et comédi ex ómnibus priúsquam tu venires?
* Benedixique ei, et erit benedictus.
<r>℣.</r> Dóminum tuum illum constítui, et omnes fratres ejus servitúti illíus subjugávi.
<r>℟.</r> Benedixique ei, et erit benedictus.

<h>Lectio 2</h>
<c>M</c>ultis tempóribus ábfuit, ne præprópera viderétur exáctio. Nam quo indulgéntior liberálitas, eo inexcusabílior pervicácia. Unde bene secúndum Matthǽum habes, quia et sepem circúmdedit: hoc est, divínæ custódiæ munitióne vallávit, ne fácile spiritálium patéret incúrsibus bestiárum. Et fodit in ea tórcular. Quómodo intellégimus quid sit tórcular, nisi forte quia Psalmi pro torculáribus inscribúntur; eo quod in his mystéria Domínicæ passiónis, modo musti Sancto fervéntis Spíritu, redundántius æstuáverint?
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Dum exíret Jacob de terra sua, vidit glóriam Dei, et ait: Quam terríbilis est locus iste!
* Non est hic áliud, nisi domus Dei, et porta cæli.
<r>℣.</r> Vere Deus est in loco isto, et ego nesciébam.
<r>℟.</r> Non est hic áliud, nisi domus Dei, et porta cæli.

<h>Reading 2</h>
Continuation of the Holy Gospel according to Matthew
<r>Matt 21:33-46</r>
<c>I</c>n that time, Jesus said to the multitude of Jews and the chief priests: Hear ye another parable. There was a man an householder, who planted a vineyard, and made a hedge round about it. And so on.

Homily by St. Ambrose, Bishop <n>of Milan.</n>
<r>Bk. ix on Luke xx</r>
<c>M</c>any derive diverse spiritual meanings from the term vineyard, but Isaias giveth us to know that the vineyard of the Lord of Sabaoth is the house of Israel. <n>v. 7.</n> Who but God planted that vineyard? He it was that let it out to husbandmen, and went into a far country; not that the Lord, Who is everywhere present, moveth from place to place; but because He is nigh unto them that seek Him, and from such as regard Him not He standeth afar off. For a long time He tarried away, lest He might seem to ask too early for the fruits of His vineyard. For where kindness is greatest, there ingratitude is worst. Therefore it is well written in Matthew, for our instruction, that He hedged it round about, that is, He girded it with the fortifications of His own Divine protection, that it might not easily lie open to the ravages of spiritual wild beasts. And digged a wine-press in it. What sense are we to put upon the wine-press, unless it be that the Psalms are here described under that title, because in them the mysteries of the Lord's Passion flow over like new wine, working under the power of the Holy Ghost? Whence also, they upon whom the Holy Ghost was outpoured were deemed to be drunken <n>Acts ii. 13.</n>. God therefore digged a wine-press, whereinto the reasonable grapes of inward fruitfulness poured their spiritual richness.
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> As Jacob went out from his own land, he saw the glory of God, and said: How dreadful is this place.
* This is none other but the house of God and this is the gate of heaven.
<r>℣.</r> Surely God is in this place, and I knew it not.
<r>℟.</r> This is none other but the house of God and this is the gate of heaven.

<h>Lectio 3</h>
<c>D</c>énique ébrii putabántur, quibus Spíritus Sanctus inundábat. Ergo et hic fodit tórcular, in quod uvæ rationábilis fructus intérior spiritáli infusióne deflúeret. Ædificávit turrim, vérticem scílicet legis attóllens: atque ita hanc víneam munítam, instrúctam, ornátam, locávit Judǽis. Et témpore frúctuum sérvulos misit. Bene tempus frúctuum pósuit, non provéntuum. Nullus enim fructus éxstitit Judæórum, nullus víneæ hujus provéntus, de qua Dóminus ait: Exspectávi ut fáceret uvas, fecit autem spinas.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Si Dóminus Deus meus fúerit mecum in via ista, per quam ego ámbulo, et custodíerit me, et déderit mihi panem ad edéndum, et vestiméntum quo opériar, et revocáverit me cum salúte:
* Erit mihi Dóminus in refúgium, et lapis iste in signum.
<r>℣.</r> Surgens ergo mane Jacob, tulit lápidem quem supposúerat cápiti suo, et eréxit in títulum, fundénsque óleum désuper, dixit.
<r>℟.</r> Erit mihi Dóminus in refúgium, et lapis iste in signum.
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
<r>℟.</r> Erit mihi Dóminus in refúgium, et lapis iste in signum.

<h>Reading 3</h>
<c>T</c>herefore it is well written in Matthew, for our instruction, that He hedged it round about, that is, He girded it with the fortifications of His own Divine protection, that it might not easily lie open to the ravages of spiritual wild beasts. And digged a wine-press in it. What sense are we to put upon the wine-press, unless it be that the Psalms are here described under that title, because in them the mysteries of the Lord's Passion flow over like new wine, working under the power of the Holy Ghost? Whence also, they upon whom the Holy Ghost was outpoured were deemed to be drunken <n>Acts ii. 13.</n>. God therefore digged a wine-press, whereinto the reasonable grapes of inward fruitfulness poured their spiritual richness. And built a tower that is, He raised up the goodly structure of the Law. And so this His vineyard, thus fortified, furnished, and garnished, He gave over to the Jews. And when the time of the fruit drew near, He sent His servants to the husbandmen. Well doth He call it the time of the fruit, not the time of the in-gathering. For the Jews yielded Him no fruit; the Lord had no ingathering from that vineyard of which He said: When I looked that it should bring forth grapes, it brought forth wild grapes. <n>Isa. v. 4.</n> Not that wine that maketh glad the heart of man, not with the new wine of the spirit, reeked that wine-press, but with the blood of the Prophets, brutally shed.
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> If the Lord my God will be with me, in this way that I go, and will keep me, and will give me bread to eat, and raiment to put on, and will bring me again safely.
* The Lord shall be my refuge, and this stone shall be a sign.
<r>℣.</r> So Jacob rose up early in the morning, and took the stone that he had put for his pillow, and set it up for a pillar, and poured oil upon the top of it, and said:
<r>℟.</r> The Lord shall be my refuge, and this shall be a sign.
<r>℣.</r> Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
<r>℟.</r> The Lord shall be my refuge, and this shall be a sign.

b.2fa327d7a5:
<h>Martyrologium</h>
<c>T</c>értio Kaléndas Mártii Luna vicésima prima. Anno Dómini 2027
<h>I</h>nsulæ, in Aprútio, sancti Gabriélis a Vírgine Perdolénte, Clérici Congregatiónis a Cruce et Passióne Dómini nuncupátæ, et Confessóris; qui, magnis intra breve vitæ spátium méritis et post mortem miráculis clarus, a Benedícto Papa Décimo quinto in Sanctórum cánonem relátus est.
<h>R</h>omæ natális sanctórum Mártyrum Alexándri, Abúndii, Antígoni et Fortunáti.
<h>A</h>lexandríæ pássio sancti Iuliáni Mártyris, qui, cum ita pódagra constríctus esset, ut neque incédere neque stare posset, una cum duóbus fámulis, qui eum in sella gestábant, Júdici offértur; quorum alter fidem negávit, alter, nómine Eunus, cum dómino suo perdurávit in confessióne Christi. Ipse porro Iuliánus et Eunus, camélis impósiti, per totam urbem circumdúci iubéntur, et flagris laniári, ac tandem, incénso rogo, hinc inde spectánte pópulo, combúri.
<h>I</h>bídem sancti Besæ mílitis, qui, cum insultántes in prædíctos Mártyres cohibéret, delátus est ad Júdicem, et, pro fide constánter agens, cápite truncátus.
<h>H</h>íspali, in Hispánia, natális sancti Leándri, ejúsdem civitátis Epíscopi, qui, sanctórum Isidóri Epíscopi ac Florentínæ Vírginis frater, sua prædicatióne et indústria gentem Visigothórum, adjuvánte Reccarédo, eórum Rege, ab Ariána impietáte ad cathólicam fidem convértit.
<h>C</h>onstantinópoli sanctórum Confessórum Basilíi et Procópii, qui, témpore Leónis Imperatóris, pro cultu sanctárum Imáginum strénue decertárunt.
<h>L</h>ugdúni, in Gállia, sancti Baldoméri Subdiaconi, viri Deo devóti, cujus sepúlcrum crebris miráculis illustrátur.
<r>℣.</r> Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.
b.de1f7e32c7:
<h>Martyrology</h>
<c>F</c>ebruary 27th 2027, the 21st day of the Moon, were born into the better life:
<h>A</h>t Rome, the holy martyrs Alexander, Abundius, Antigonus, and Fortunatus.
<h>A</h>t Alexandria, [in the year 250,] the holy martyr Julian. He was so crippled by the gout that he could neither walk nor stand, and was carried before the judge in a chair by two servants. Of these two servants one denied the faith the other, whose name was Eunus, persisted in confessing Christ along with Julian. They were both placed upon camels and led about the whole city, lashed, and at length publicly burnt upon a pyre.
<h>T</h>here also the holy soldier Besas. He rebuked some who were jeering at the martyrs aforenamed, for which cause he was accused before the judge, and as he stood firm in the faith he was beheaded.
<h>A</h>t Seville, in Spain, [in the year 596,] holy Leander, Bishop of that city, by whose preaching and labours, assisted by Reccared, King of the Visigoths, that nation were converted from the Arian misbelief to the Catholic faith.
<h>A</h>t Constantinople, [in 750] the holy Confessors Basil and Procopius, who in the time of the Emperor Leo the Isaurian, contended valiantly for the honouring of holy images.

<c>C</c>onvertímini ad me in toto corde vestro, in jejúnio, et fletu, et planctu. Et scíndite corda vestra, et non vestiménta vestra, ait Dóminus omnípotens.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>Hymnus</r>
<c>A</c>udi, benígne Cónditor,
Nostras preces cum flétibus,
In hoc sacro jejúnio
Fusas quadragenário.

<h>S</h>crutátor alme córdium,
Infírma tu scis vírium:
Ad te revérsis éxhibe
Remissiónis grátiam.

<h>M</h>ultum quidem peccávimus,
Sed parce confiténtibus:
Ad laudem tui nóminis
Confer medélam lánguidis.

<h>S</h>ic corpus extra cónteri
Dona per abstinéntiam,
Ieiúnet ut mens sóbria
A labe prorsus críminum.

<h>P</h>ræsta, beáta Trínitas,
Concéde, simplex Únitas;
Ut fructuósa sint tuis
Ieiuniórum múnera.
Amen.

<r>℟.</r> Ut custódiant te in ómnibus viis tuis.
b.36ea047503:

<c>B</c>e converted to me with all your heart, in fasting, and in weeping, and in mourning. And rend your hearts, and not your garments, said the almighty Lord.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>Hymn</r>
<c>O</c> kind Creator, bow thine ear
To mark the cry, to know the tear
Before thy throne of mercy spent
In this thy holy fast of Lent.

<h>O</h>ur hearts are open, Lord, to thee:
Thou knowest our infirmity;
Pour out on all who seek thy face
Abundance of thy pardoning grace.

<h>O</h>ur sins are many, this we know;
Spare us, good Lord, thy mercy show;
And for the honour of thy name
Our fainting souls to life reclaim.

<h>G</h>ive us the self-control that springs
From discipline of outward things,
That fasting inward secretly
The soul may purely dwell with thee.

<h>W</h>e pray thee, Holy Trinity,
One God, unchanging Unity,
That we from this our abstinence
May reap the fruits of penitence.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> God hath given His Angels charge over thee.
<r>℟.</r> To keep thee in all thy ways.
